rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker failed to thank past favors by undertaking the hard passage of freeing a captive or feeding the needy, which requires self-discipline.
rows.anchor: فلم يشكر تلك الأيادي باقتحام العقبة وهو الدخول في أمر شديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountain pass is a metaphor for a difficult undertaking, here explained by emancipation and feeding the needy.
rows.anchor: العقبة الطريق في الجبل استعارها بما فسرها عز وجل من الفلك والإطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coordinated negation لا suits several intended acts, unlike لم, since freeing and feeding are normally repeated deeds.
rows.anchor: لتعدد المراد بها حسن وقوع لا موقع لم فإنها لا تكاد تقع إلا مكررة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The terms derive respectively from hunger, kinship closeness, and poverty.
rows.anchor: والمسغبة والمقربة والمتربة مفعلات من سغب إذا جاع وقرب في النسب وترب إذا افتقر

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي
rows.claim: They read فك رقبة أو أطعم as a grammatical substitute for اقتحم.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي فك رقبة أو أطعم على الإبدال من اقتحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parenthetical question stresses that the listener cannot grasp the pass's difficulty and reward.
rows.anchor: اعترض معناه إنك لم تدركنه صعوبتها وثوابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ثم connects faith to undertaking the pass or freeing a captive, marking faith's higher rank and its role as a condition for other obediences.
rows.anchor: عطفه على اقتحم أو فك ب ثم لتباعد الإيمان عن العتق والإطعام في الرتبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They urged one another to remain patient in obeying God.
rows.anchor: وأوصي بعضهم بعضا بالصبر على طاعة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mercy means compassion toward God's servants.
rows.anchor: بالرحمة على عباده أو بموجبات رحمة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, mercy means acts that bring about God's mercy.
rows.anchor: بالرحمة على عباده أو بموجبات رحمة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading is that God made the human being one of the people of Hell.
rows.anchor: بأن جعلناه من أهل النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the lowest of the low is Hell itself.
rows.anchor: أو إلى أسفل سافلين وهو النار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An anonymous view identifies the lowest of the low as extreme old age.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو أرذل العمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception of believers who do good deeds is a disconnected exception.
rows.anchor: فيكون قوله( إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ) استثناء منقطعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reward does not end.
rows.anchor: ( فلهم أجر غير ممنون ) لا ينقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, no one will hold the reward over them as a favor.
rows.anchor: أو لا يمن به عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first sense of an unending reward, this clause establishes and confirms the result of the exception.
rows.anchor: وهو على الأولى حكم مرتب على الاستثناء مقرر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His scales are heavy because the measures of the kinds of his good deeds outweigh.
rows.anchor: بأن ترجحت مقادير أنواع حسناته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The life is endowed with satisfaction.
rows.anchor: في عيش راضية ذات رضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the life is pleasing to its inhabitant.
rows.anchor: راضية ذات رضا ،   أو مرضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His scales are light because he has no good deed worthy of consideration.
rows.anchor: بأن لم يكن له حسنة يعبأ بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, his evil deeds outweigh his good deeds.
rows.anchor: أو ترجحت سيئاته على حسناته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His abode is the burning Fire, which is named al-Hāwiya.
rows.anchor: النار المحرقة ،   والهاوية من أسمائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following question, “what will make you know what it is,” points back to al-Hāwiya.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قال { وما أدراك ما هيه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra's place of revelation is disputed, and it has eight verses.
rows.anchor: سورة التكاثر مختلف فيها ،   وآيها ثماني آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alhākum means it occupied or distracted you; the root conveys turning toward pastime and derives from lahā, to be heedless.
rows.anchor: ألهاكم : شغلكم ،   وأصله الصرف إلى اللهو ،   منقول من لها إذا غفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-takāthur means boasting over abundance.
rows.anchor: منقول من لها إذا غفل .   التكاثر : التباهي بالكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once they had counted all the living, they turned to the graves and boasted of the dead; visiting graves figuratively describes recalling the dead.
rows.anchor: إذا استوعبتم عدد الأحياء صرتم إلى المقابر

rows.speaker: رُوي
rows.claim: Banū ʿAbd Manāf first outnumbered Banū Sahm; Sahm then proposed counting both living and dead, and claimed superiority.
rows.anchor: روي أن بني عبد مناف وبني سهم تفاخروا بالكثرة

rows.speaker: بنو سهم
rows.claim: Banū Sahm said rivalry had destroyed them in the pre-Islamic age and challenged their rivals to count the living and dead.
rows.anchor: فقال بنو سهم : إن البغي أهلكنا في الجاهلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of distraction—the religious matters that concern them—is omitted for grandeur and emphasis.
rows.anchor: وإنما حذف المنهي عنه وهو ما يعنيهم من أمر الدين للتعظيم والمبالغة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the rivalry over wealth and children as lasting until death and burial, wasting life that should have prepared for the afterlife; visiting graves means dying.
rows.anchor: ألهاكم التكاثر بالأموال والأولاد إلى أن متم وقبرتم مضيعين أعماركم في طلب الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause may substitute for كل, or it may be a nominative or accusative expression of blame.
rows.anchor: { الذي جمع مالا } بدل من كل أو ذم منصوب أو مرفوع

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read ʿaddadahu with a doubled consonant, signaling repeated counting or accumulation as provisions for calamities.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي بالتشديد للتكثير وعدده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doubled form can mean counting the wealth again and again.
rows.anchor: أو عده مرة بعد أخرى

rows.speaker: قُرئ
rows.claim: A reading that separates the assimilation supports the doubled reading.
rows.anchor: ويؤيده أنه قرئ ( وعدده ) على فك الإدغام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He thinks his money has left him immortal in this world, and loves it as he would love immortality.
rows.anchor: { يحسب أن ماله أخلده } تركه خالدا في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, love of wealth has distracted him from death.
rows.anchor: أو حب المال أغفله عن الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, his long hopes made him expect immortality and act as though death would not come.
rows.anchor: أو طول أمله حتى حسب أنه مخلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse alludes to striving for the afterlife as the path to lasting life.
rows.anchor: وفيه تعريض بأن المخلد هو السعي للآخرة

none: The scan page contains front matter, contents headings, and stray OCR fragments, with no legible tafsir exposition.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about the pass stirs curiosity; emancipation is the first pass, associated with chastity, generosity, and disciplining appetite.
rows.anchor: وكان الإنسان أشهى ما إليه تعرف ما أشكل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using “release” rather than complete emancipation includes the smallest possible aid, even a small contribution toward freedom.
rows.anchor: معبراً بالفك الذي هو أدنى ما يكون من العتق لأنه الإعانة فيه ولو بما قل

rows.speaker: البراء رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: A report attributed to al-Barāʾ distinguishes freeing a person outright from helping pay the price of release.
rows.anchor: كما ورد في حديث البراء رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Complete emancipation means freeing the person oneself, whereas release can mean contributing to the price.
rows.anchor: وعتقها أن تفرد بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Release includes relief from captivity, injustice, debt, or sickness, out of gratitude and compassion rather than display, reward-seeking, or fear.
rows.anchor: أي من الأسر أو الظلم أو الغرم أو السقم شكراً لمن أولاه الخير وتنفيساً للكربة حباً للمعالي والمكارم لا رياء وسمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These deeds signal sound temperament, high aspiration, noble character, and restraint; their occurrence before faith reveals innate purity and readiness to obey.
rows.anchor: تدل على جودة الطبع وعلو الهمة وكرم العنصر وإباء النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Then marks faith as a later, second pass that purifies the rational faculty through wisdom.
rows.anchor: بأداة التراخي في قوله مشيراً إلى العقبة الثانية وهي الحكمة المزكية للقوة النطقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deeds may precede conversion or occur at Islam's beginnings, showing pure origin; he accepted guidance without pride at becoming a follower after leading.
rows.anchor: بعد التخلق بهذه الأخلاق الزاكية العالية النفيسة الغالية في حال كفره أو مبادىء إسلامه للدلالة على صفاء جبلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The convert corrects his judgment and realizes that following the guide raises him from a supposed high position to greater heights.
rows.anchor: ولم تحمله حمية الأنف وشماخة النفس على الإباء عن أن يكون تابعاً بعد ما كان متبوعاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ascent to insight and high rank recalls the signs for people of understanding in Ṭā Hā 20:54 and 20:128.
rows.anchor: إن في ذلك لآيات لأولي النهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Bakr exemplifies this virtue: the author ranks him immediately after the prophets because he displayed these deeds before Islam.
rows.anchor: ولذلك كان الصديق رضي الله تعالى عنه أعلى الناس درجة بعد النبيين

rows.speaker: ابن الدغنة
rows.claim: When Ibn al-Dughunnah found Abū Bakr leaving Mecca after persecution, he praised his kinship, hospitality, care for the burdened, and help in hardship.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الدغنة حين وجده قد خرج من مكة المشرفة يريد الهجرة

rows.speaker: خديجة رضي الله عنها
rows.claim: The author says Khadīja gave the Prophet the same reassurance and praise when he returned trembling after Gabriel appeared.
rows.anchor: كما قالت خديجة رضي الله عنها للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حين رجع إليها ترجف بوادره من تجلي جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With divine guidance Abū Bakr answered the call immediately, without hesitation, and rose to the highest ranks of Islam.
rows.anchor: وشرب من صافي مشربه توفيقاً من الله تعالى لم يتلعثم حين دعاه إلى الدين

rows.speaker: أبو بكر رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: At al-Ḥudaybiyya Abū Bakr told ʿUmar what the Prophet had said, word for word, despite not having heard it from him.
rows.anchor: قال يوم الحديبية لعمر رضي الله عنهما حين أظهر الكراهة للصلح ما قال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سواء حرفاً بحرف

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abū Bakr never drank wine; he said he would spend all his wealth on anything that increased his intellect, not on something that removed it.
rows.anchor: وكان إذا ليم على ذلك في الجاهلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praised deeds are valid only with faith: later faith embraces pre-conversion deeds, while deeds after faith plainly depend on it.
rows.anchor: وتلك الأعمال لا تصح وإن كانت ممدوحة في كل حال إلا بالإيمان

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said to a convert, “You have accepted Islam with the good you did before.”
rows.anchor: كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith raises people from humiliation, moves them to excellent conduct, and leads to the demanding religious laws that oppose natural inclinations.
rows.anchor: حاملاً له على محاسن الأعمال ومكارم الأفعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The struggle against one's nature requires courage; because patience is bitter and cannot endure alone, believers encourage each other through acts of obedience and enjoining right.
rows.anchor: وكان الصبر لمرارته لا يدوم إلا بالتعاون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The required patience reaches from enjoining right through dangerous deeds; courage is proverbial as an hour's patience.
rows.anchor: فإن الشجاعة كما قيل صبر ساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because conflict can harden people, mercy is a fruit of endurance and justice, a fourth pass that moderates between excess and deficiency.
rows.anchor: فكانت الرحمة من ثمرات الاصطبار المثمر للعدالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the verb “they urged one another” emphasizes how few people practice mercy.
rows.anchor: مؤكداً بإعادة العامل إشارة إلى قلة العاملين بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cultivate great mercy suited to its time and place, orienting themselves toward what brings divine love and aversion for God's sake.
rows.anchor: الرحمة العظيمة بحسب زمانها ومكانها بأن يوطنوا أنفسهم على كل ما يحمل على الرحمة العظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before faith they were free of ostentation and self-admiration and ready for purification; faith purified them into full illumination and knowledge.
rows.anchor: لأنهم كانوا قبل الإيمان خالصين عن الرياء والإعجاب متهيئين للتزكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though endowed with excellent form, humans face desires and ignoble traits that ruin most of them; this displays God's power and applies to the species as a whole.
rows.anchor: وكان أكثر الخلق بها هالكاً لتتبين قدرة الله سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Then marks how remote the corruption is from the sound reason and clear mind with which humanity began.
rows.anchor: بأداة التراخي على أن اعوجاجه بعد ذلك العقل الرصين والذهن الصافي المستنير في غاية البعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's return of the human being disables the intended benefits of his faculties, so he wastes himself and loses the means to happiness.
rows.anchor: فضيع نفسه وفوت أساب سعادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lowest of the low is beneath inert, filthy matter; evil acts turn an initially well-composed nature toward utter disorder.
rows.anchor: أي إلى ما تحت رتبة الجمادات المستقذرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Desires overpower reason, leading people to worship beings below themselves and to commit injustice, falsehood, and grave sins.
rows.anchor: فغلبت على عقله فأعمته حتى أوردته الموارد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Misusing reason and other divinely given faculties makes humans lower than beasts and insects, which have no reason for desire to obscure.
rows.anchor: فصار بذلك أحط رتبة من البهائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People misuse the faculties given for their purpose and thus deserve humiliating punishment.
rows.anchor: فاستعمل ما خلقناه له من الآلات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since many die without recompense for their deeds, divine wisdom requires resurrection and lasting punishment after it.
rows.anchor: ثم يموت من غير مجازاة على شيء من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Physical decline also returns people low: old age weakens them after strength, strips honor and knowledge, and makes former companions recoil.
rows.anchor: وأما في خلقه فبالهرم حتى صار بعد تلك القوى ضعيفاً

rows.speaker: ابن برجان
rows.claim: Ibn Barjān reads the return as disbelief in religion, metamorphosis in the intermediate realm to the animal form matching one's character and deeds, and a disfigured form in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن برجان : أما رده في طريق الديانة فبالكفر والتكذيب

rows.speaker: الإمام أبو العباس الأقليشي
rows.claim: Al-Aqīlishī says the body pulls humans downward: reason over desire raises them to the highest realm, while desire over reason lowers them to Hell.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو العباس الأقليشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prior judgment concerns most of humanity, while the righteous are a very small group and form the exception.
rows.anchor: ولما حكم بهذا الرد على جميع النوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers in God and His messengers have insight; divine gentleness lets reason, aided by original nature, overcome desire and protects them from decrepit old age.
rows.anchor: أي بالله ورسله فكانوا من ذوي البصائر والمعارف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As age increases, their reason's light grows while desire and attachment to this world weaken and their spiritual insight strengthens.
rows.anchor: فكانوا كلما زدناهم سناً زدنا أنوار عقولهم ونقصنا نار شهواتهم بما أضعفنا من إحكام طبائعهم وتعلقهم بهذا العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good works confirm a true claim to faith and are beautiful deeds rooted in faith and perfected through divinely granted knowledge.
rows.anchor: من محاسن الأعمال من الأقوال والأفعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God preserves this small group on the original nature of the best form, keeping desire from tainting it, so they follow the messengers and embody justice, beneficence, and noble conduct.
rows.anchor: بما كملناهم به وشرفناهم على جميع الحيوانات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage uses iḥtibāk: evil deeds and their punishment are implicit in the first clause, while preservation in the original fitra is implicit in the exception.
rows.anchor: فالآية كما ترى من الاحتباك : حذف أولاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reward is immense and lasts without interruption.
rows.anchor: وهو مع ذلك { غير ممنون * } أي مقطوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God does not hold the reward over them as a favor, even in illness or old age.
rows.anchor: أو يمن عليهم به حتى في حالة المرض والهرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They sincerely resolve never to omit a good deed; when old age makes them unable, they still receive the reward for what they did in health.
rows.anchor: وعزموا عزماً صادقاً أنهم لا ينقصون من أعمال البر ذرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reward answers their actions, yet both its basis and its extension are God's grace; those who follow desire downward face great punishment.
rows.anchor: فضلاً منه بالأصل والفرع حتى أنهم إذا عجزوا بالهرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since a day is described by what happens in it, the discourse now distinguishes the people's outcomes.
rows.anchor: ولما كان اليوم إنما يوصف لأجل ما يقع فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scales become heavy through outweighing.
rows.anchor: { فأما من ثقلت } أي بالرجحان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural reflects the many kinds of good deeds done by following truth and avoiding falsehood; the weighed objects are deeds embodied and their records.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت الموزونات كثيرة الأنواع جداً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The things weighed are both the deeds themselves, given bodily form, and their written records.
rows.anchor: والموزون الأعمال أنفسها تجسداً وصحائفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessed life is a life in which its inhabitant continually moves and lives.
rows.anchor: حسناته { في عيشة } أي حياة تتقلب فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine form suggests a single, constant state of clarity and pleasure rather than the varied conditions of worldly life.
rows.anchor: ولعله ألحقها الهاء الدالة على الوحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The life either possesses satisfaction or is pleasing; its abode is the lofty Garden.
rows.anchor: { راضية * } أي ذات رضى ،   أو مرضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scales are light or unsteady because his evil deeds predominate, or because he has no good deed through following falsehood.
rows.anchor: { موازينه * } أي بأن غلبت سيئاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falsehood felt light to him in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وخفته عليه في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His “mother” is what shelters and embraces him; earth and a dwelling are called mother because one seeks and rests in them.
rows.anchor: أي التي تؤويه وتضمه إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse suggests he was created from Hell and dominated by a satanic, fiery nature.
rows.anchor: وهو يفهم أنه مخلوق منها غلب عليه طبع الشيطان لكون العنصر الناري أكثر أجزائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite description magnifies the place and indicates it offers no rest or stable ground.
rows.anchor: وعظمها بالتنكير والتعبير بالوصف المعلم بأنه لا قرار لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Hāwiya is an extremely low, descending fire in which he keeps falling; the passage omits a hostile life in the second clause and a mother in the first.
rows.anchor: أي نار نازلة سافلة جداً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After al-Qāriʿa establishes the Hour, divides people into wretched and happy, and ends with the wretched, this sūra opens with the cause of misery to warn listeners away from it.
rows.anchor: لما أثبت في القارعة أمر الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alhākum means that this rivalry deeply distracted nearly everyone.
rows.anchor: أي أغفلكم - إلا النادر منكم - غفلة عظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-takāthur is boasting over plentiful, perishable worldly goods such as wealth, rank, and children.
rows.anchor: وهو المباهاة والمفاخرة بكثرة الأعراض الفانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rivalry consumes effort in gathering and distracts from death, the afterlife, true religion, remembrance of God, and competing in saving acts.
rows.anchor: فصرفكم ذلك إلى اللهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ignorance born of desire, self-love, and love of ease keeps people from submitting, so their scales grow light.
rows.anchor: لأنكم لا تسلمون بما غلب عليكم من الجهل الذي سببه شهوة النفس وحب الراحة فخفت موازينكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of distraction is left unstated to magnify what they neglect and suggest nothing is more grievous to neglect.
rows.anchor: وحذف هذا الشيء الملهو عنه لتعظيمه والدلالة على أنه ليس غيره مما يؤسف على اللهو عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling burial a visit answers deniers who imagined permanent residence in graves and signals that resurrection must follow.
rows.anchor: ويعتقدون دوام الإقامة في القبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a long stay in the intermediate realm is brief beside lasting residence in Paradise or Hell; a visitor eventually returns to a settled home.
rows.anchor: وأن اللبث في البرزخ وإن طال فإنما هو كلبث الزائر عند مزوره في جنب الإقامة بعد البعث في دار النعيم أو غار الجحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They visit graves through dying and burial, when the time for deeds that save them has passed; death alone should deter them even before the greater events of judgment.
rows.anchor: لا تتمكنون من عمل ما ينجيكم

rows.speaker: أعرابي
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān reports that a Bedouin heard the verse and inferred resurrection, since a visitor departs rather than stays.
rows.anchor: سمع بعض الأعراب الآية فقال

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: Ibn Abī al-Dunyā reports that ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said the graves are only a visit and one must return home, to Paradise or Hell.
rows.anchor: عن عمر بن عبد العزيز أنه قرأها ثم قال

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links the sūra to the preceding al-Qāriʿa: rivalry in numbers, kin, and family distracts from preparing for its terrors and is followed by threats.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the repeated threats reinforce the rebuke; the omitted answer is that certain knowledge would have stopped their rivalry, and an implicit oath answers that they will see Hell.
rows.anchor: كلا سوف تعلمون ثم كلا سوف تعلمون

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that if people knew what he knew, they would laugh little and weep much.
rows.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wealthy who needlessly hoard are especially blameworthy in a culture that treats accumulation as success and boasts of profit; this description exposes the true loser.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الذي يفعل النقيصة من غير حاجة تحوجه إليها

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers double the consonant in jamaʿa to signal abundant accumulation; others lighten it because the basic verb already conveys collecting.
rows.anchor: جاء التشديد في فعله لأبي جعفر وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unaugmented form of collecting inherently indicates abundance, unlike counting, which can refer to a small number.
rows.anchor: مطلق الجمع يدل على الكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All readers agree on doubling ʿaddada because the undoubled form can refer to counting only a few things.
rows.anchor: ولهذا أجمعوا على التضعيف فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wealth is great, and repeated counting stresses its abundance.
rows.anchor: وأكد مراد الكثرة بقوله : { وعدده }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He either keeps so much that counting it takes a long time or hoards it as a reserve against worldly troubles.
rows.anchor: أي جعله بحيث إذا أريد عدده طال الزمان فيه وكثر التعداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may be read as a resumption.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون استئنافاً ،   وفيه تعريض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because his intellect is deficient, he thinks his counted wealth grants him worldly immortality and loves it as he loves eternal life.
rows.anchor: لقلة عقله { أن ماله } أي ذلك الذي عدده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, this is a metonym for living as if death will never come: he immerses himself in sin, turns from God, and pursues fleeting pleasures.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ذلك كناية عن أنه عمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse alludes to lasting life being gained only through righteous deeds that bring felicity in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وفيه تعريض بأنه لا يفيد الخلد إلا الأعمال الصالحة المسعدة في الدار الآخرة
